## 2. Streams — every `w.*` accessor

`w` is the `&mut StrategyWiring<'_>` passed to `GraphStrategy::configure`. Every method below is extracted from `StrategyWiring`'s public inherent impl blocks (`backtest-engine/crates/bt-core/src/graph_engine/wiring.rs`), so this list cannot drift from what the compiler actually accepts.

### Source accessors (the market + the engine reporting back to you)

| Call | Returns | `PayloadKind` of the element | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `w.quotes(..)` | `Stream<Quote>` | State | Instrument 0's quote source (alias of `quotes_of(0)`). |
| `w.trades(..)` | `Stream<Trade>` | Queue | The trade tape for instrument 0 (single-instrument runs). Queue payload: consume via `iter_fresh()`. Empty forever on runs constructed without a trade feed. |
| `w.wakes(..)` | `Stream<Wake>` | Queue | The strategy's private wake stream (spec §7.4) — already a triggering input of the strategy node; read tags with `ctx.s(handle).iter_fresh()`. |
| `w.portfolio(..)` | `Stream<Portfolio>` | State | The run's portfolio stream (M4d): equity, realized PnL, position, and trade count at own-order knowledge time. Sub or peek it like any stream — no more hand-tracking fills in strategy state. |
| `w.residuals(..)` | `Stream<crate::exec::Residual>` | Queue | Executor stand-down reports (spec §8): a [`crate::exec::Residual`] arrives here one epoch after the executor gave up short of target. Empty forever on runs without an executor. |
| `w.timer(..)` | `Stream<TimerTick>` | Queue | Register a bounded periodic timer (M5-era timer sources, landed): the engine creates an epoch at every tick timestamp and delivers a [`TimerTick`] on the returned stream — bars close at exact boundaries, strategies fire periodically without a `WakeAt` round trip. Pure source: timer-driven features are recordable. |

Rendered call signatures, verbatim from rustdoc:

- `fn quotes(&self) -> Stream<Quote>`
- `fn trades(&self) -> Stream<Trade>`
- `fn wakes(&self) -> Stream<Wake>`
- `fn portfolio(&self) -> Stream<Portfolio>`
- `fn residuals(&self) -> Stream<crate::exec::Residual>`
- `fn timer(&mut self, spec: TimerSpec) -> Stream<TimerTick>`

**A run is single-instrument** (see SKILL.md). `quotes_of`/`trades_of`/`portfolio_of`/`instrument`/`instruments` exist on `StrategyWiring` for basket runs; `quotes_of(0)`/`trades_of(0)`/`portfolio_of(0)` are aliases of the plain calls above, and any other index panics inside `configure` under the single-instrument executor this path builds. Do not call them with a nonzero index.

### Composition and other wiring calls

SKILL.md documents `add`, `sub` and `peek` as the calls this authoring path needs. The rest below exist on `StrategyWiring` too, but for basket runs, shared/recorded lanes, and the feed catalog — engine lanes this single-instrument path does not build. They are listed for completeness, not as calls to reach for; if you believe you need one that is not `add`/`sub`/`peek`, say so rather than guessing — an invented call costs a whole build slot to discover.

| Call | Signature | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `w.add` | `fn add(&mut self, node: N) -> Stream<N::Output>` | Compose a feature node (CSE applies). On a shared run (auto-partition), a declaration the [`SharedFeatureSet`] recorded binds to its column transparently instead of computing live. |
| `w.add_model` | `fn add_model(&mut self, node: ModelNode<F>) -> Stream<Forecast>` | Compose a [`ModelNode`] and declare its artifact identity for the run's model lineage (Phase 6 WS3a). Records `node.artifact_id()` (in declaration order, for [`GraphEngine::model_artifact_ids`]) and then delegates to [`Self::add`] — so a `ModelNode` participates in CSE, shared-run binding, and every other wiring path exactly like any other feature node; the extra step is purely recording which model artifacts this run depends on. |
| `w.component` | `fn component(&mut self, module: &str, version: &str, export: &str, inputs: &[crate::chart::ResolvedInput], config: &[u8]) -> Result<crate::registry::ComponentOutputs, BuildError>` | Instantiate a pinned component and receive its outputs as streams (map #251 step 5, resolving [#285]). |
| `w.instrument` | `fn instrument(&self, id: bt_model::identifiers::InstrumentId) -> Option<&bt_model::Instrument>` | The run's [`bt_model::Instrument`] with this id — the same definition the venue validates orders against, so a strategy can size its orders to the instrument's `size_precision`/ `size_increment` (e.g. via [`bt_model::Instrument::make_qty`]) instead of guessing a precision the venue will reject. `None` when the id is not among the run's instruments — and always `None` on probe builds (catalog requirements probe, shared-sweep recording probe), which configure the graph but never execute orders, so a strategy must treat a miss as "sizing unknown", not an error. |
| `w.instruments` | `fn instruments(&self) -> &[bt_model::Instrument]` | Every instrument this run trades, in feed order. |
| `w.peek` | `fn peek(&mut self, h: Stream<T>, depth: u32) -> Stream<T>` | Register a read-only (peek) input: readable, never wakes. |
| `w.port` | `fn port(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Stream<T>, BuildError>` | Resolve a catalog port by name + type (feed-catalog spec §3): a venue port resolves as its quote stream, a stream port as its source stream. Checks **name → role → payload tag** in that order, so the error names the first mismatch, and records the port into the run's resolved set (§7) on success. Fails with [`BuildError::Port`] — an unknown name, a `reference`-role port, or a payload-type mismatch — listing every available port so the error is self-diagnosing (§8). |
| `w.portfolio_for` | `fn portfolio_for(&mut self, name: &str) -> Result<Stream<Portfolio>, BuildError>` | Resolve a venue port's portfolio stream by name (feed-catalog spec §3): the by-name replacement for `portfolio_of(idx)`. Venue ports only — a stream or reference port is a [`BuildError::Port`] with role detail (§8). Records the port into the resolved set (§7) on success, like `port`/`reference` — `&mut self` (not `&self`) exists for this. |
| `w.portfolio_of` | `fn portfolio_of(&self, idx: usize) -> Stream<Portfolio>` | Portfolio stream for instrument `idx`: global equity/realized/ trades with that instrument's position (v1.13). |
| `w.quotes_of` | `fn quotes_of(&self, idx: usize) -> Stream<Quote>` | Quote source for instrument `idx` (feed order, v1.13). |
| `w.recorded` | `fn recorded(&mut self, col: &Arc<RecordedColumn<T>>) -> Stream<T>` | Bind a recorded column (§7.6) as a source in this run's graph. The column's measured initialization boundary and stream metadata are carried over (`source_with_warmup_and_meta` — the replay-fidelity rule), so consumers fire exactly when their live twins would and report the same provenance/unit. Subscribe the returned handle like any stream. |
| `w.reference` | `fn reference(&mut self, name: &str, expected_subject: SubjectId) -> Result<Arc<T>, BuildError>` | Resolve a reference port as a subject-checked `Arc<T>` (feed-catalog spec §3): the strategy states the `SubjectId` it expects (typically a venue port's instrument), and resolution fails with [`BuildError::Port`] on an unknown name, a non-reference role, a type mismatch, or `table.subject() != expected_subject` — turning the wrong-instrument hazard into a structural build error. Records the port into the resolved set (§7) on success. Reference handles are strategy-scope only (§3); as-of reads take the epoch clock at the read site. |
| `w.sub` | `fn sub(&mut self, h: Stream<T>, depth: u32) -> Stream<T>` | Register a *triggering* read: emissions wake the strategy. |
| `w.trades_of` | `fn trades_of(&self, idx: usize) -> Stream<Trade>` | The trade tape for instrument `idx` (multi-instrument runs). |

`w.add(node)` is how every entry in the node catalogue (§4) gets wired in: it composes a feature node and returns a `Stream` of its output. `w.sub`/`w.peek` register a stream you already have a handle for as a triggering/read-only input and hand the same handle back — store it, you read through it later via `ctx.s(handle)`, never through `w` again.

### Reading a stream: `ctx.s(handle)` → `View`

`ctx: &GraphCtx<'_>` is what `on_update`/`on_execution` receive. `ctx.s(handle)` returns a `View<'_, T>`:

- **State** streams (`w.quotes()`, `w.portfolio()`, and every plain-`f64`/`bool`/custom-struct indicator node) are read by **indexed history**: `view[0]` is the most recent element, `view[1]` the one before it, and so on back to `view.len() - 1`. `view.len()` on a State stream is the ring's occupancy (`min(total_seen, declared_depth)`).
- **Queue** streams (`w.trades()`, `w.wakes()`, `w.residuals()`, `w.timer(..)`, and every bar/pattern/detector node) are consumed **losslessly** via `view.iter_fresh()` — every element appended since this node last fired, oldest to newest. **`iter_fresh()` panics if the stream's `PayloadKind` is `State`** (`"iter_fresh is a Queue read; use indexed history on State streams"`, `bt-core/src/graph/stream.rs`). This is exactly the mistake the evidence session made against `w.quotes()`.
- **Indexing (`view[i]`) is bounded differently per kind** — this is not symmetric, and the difference is dangerous for the stream nearly every strategy reads (`w.quotes()` is State):
  - **Queue**: bounded by *this edge's own declared depth* (the `depth` argument to `w.sub`/`w.peek`, or a node's own declared input depth). Reading past it panics naming the declaration — see fact 2 below.
  - **State**: bounded only by the ring's physical capacity, which is sized ONCE, at compile time, to the **maximum depth declared by ANY consumer of that stream** — not by what you yourself declared. If another node subscribes to the same State stream at depth 20 and you subscribed at depth 5, the ring is 20 elements deep and `view[10]` on your side does **not** panic: it silently returns real data from inside the ring that you never declared needing. Indexing past the ring's actual capacity does panic, but with a different, generic message — `"history index {i} out of range (len {N})"` (`TypedBuf::history`) — that names the ring's size, not your declaration. **Treat your own declared depth as the only bound that matters and index within it yourself; nothing enforces it for you on a State stream.**

**Two facts from `backtest-engine/CLAUDE.md` that bite (`InputSpec.depth` is load-bearing, not advisory, #371) — both are Queue-specific, which is exactly why the State behavior above needs spelling out separately:**

1. **`View::len()` over a declared Queue edge reports `min(total_produced, depth)`, NOT the retained length.** The retained length moves with `RetentionPolicy` and the run loop's 64-epoch reclamation cadence, so a loop shaped `for i in 0..v.len()` would silently fold over a different element count per policy if `len()` reported retention instead — the declared depth is the one bound stable under every policy. State rings are unaffected (`min(total, capacity)`, sized at compile time, never reclaimed) — but see the capacity-sharing hazard above.
2. **Indexing a Queue stream past the declared depth panics, naming the declaration.** `view[i]` for `i >= depth` asserts with `"history index {i} exceeds the declared lookback (depth {d}) of this Queue input … declare the depth you actually read (`w.sub(stream, {depth})`)"` (`View::history`, `bt-core/src/graph/stream.rs`) — this is a runtime abort, not a compiler error, and it names the fix. **This check does not run for a State stream** — see above.

`ctx.s(handle)` itself panics if `handle` was never given to `w.sub`/`w.peek` (or the node's own `inputs()`) — an undeclared read, caught at the first firing, not at compile time.

---

## 3. `Cmd` — the command vocabulary

> The strategy command vocabulary (spec §7.4; raw order commands — the executor layer arrives later).

Every variant, with its fields and units, from `bt-core/src/graph_engine/mod.rs`:

### `Cmd::Order (bt_model::order::OrderCommand)`

(undocumented on the variant itself)

### `Cmd::WakeAt { at: bt_model::types::UnixNanos, tag: u64 }`

(undocumented on the variant itself)

### `Cmd::WakeAfter { after: u64, tag: u64 }`

(undocumented on the variant itself)

### `Cmd::Target { qty: f64 }`

Desired signed position in lots (spec §8.3) — consumed by an
interposed executor; a run without one rejects it loudly.

### `Cmd::TargetFor { instrument_id: bt_model::identifiers::InstrumentId, qty: f64 }`

Instrument-scoped desired position for basket runs (a
`BasketExecutor` routes it; bare `Target` means instrument 0).

### `Cmd::Residual (crate::exec::Residual)`

An executor's stand-down report riding the command stream; the
engine re-injects it one epoch later on the `residuals()` stream
(feedback crosses epochs — never delivered within the emitting
epoch). A strategy emitting one simply feeds itself.

**`Cmd::target(qty)` is the constructor a strategy actually calls** (a free `impl Cmd` helper wrapping `Cmd::Target { qty }`). `qty` is the **desired signed position, in lots** — absolute, not a delta: sending `Cmd::target(5.0)` twice in a row leaves the position at 5.0 lots, not 10.0. It is idempotent — re-emitting the same value every epoch is harmless and needs no edge-detection state — pinned by `target_reaches_flattens_and_reconciliation_is_idempotent` (`bt-core/tests/suite/exec_e2e.rs`). Negative `qty` is short; `0.0` flattens. It is not notional currency and not a fraction of equity — convert explicitly (see SKILL.md's worked example).

`Cmd::target_for` is the basket form (`TargetFor { instrument_id, qty }`); under the single-instrument executor this path builds, calling it fails the run outright. `Cmd::Order`, `Cmd::WakeAt`/`Cmd::WakeAfter` and `Cmd::Residual` exist for engine-internal and basket-executor lanes — do not reach for one you have not seen used in SKILL.md or the exemplar.

## 4. The node catalogue

131 types implement `bt_core::graph::Node` (equivalently `bt_module_sdk::core::graph::Node`) and are composable with **`w.add(SomeNode::new(...))`**, which returns a `Stream<SomeNode::Output>` you then `w.sub`/`w.peek` and read through `ctx.s(...)` like any other stream (§2). **There is no `w.bars()` accessor** — a bar is a node you build by feeding `BarAggregator`/`TimerBarAggregator`/`TradeBarAggregator` a `Stream<f64>` (the quote mid, via `w.add(MidNode::new(w.quotes()))`) or `w.trades()`, not a source you subscribe to directly. This is not a gap — the aggregator IS the bar feature, wired the same way as every indicator below.

### `bars`

Feature-space (quote-mid) time bars — the ordinary way to get bar-based logic. `BarAggregator` closes on the first epoch at/after a boundary and emits nothing for empty intervals; `TimerBarAggregator` pairs with an engine timer (`w.timer(..)`) for exact boundary closes even when empty. Both are `Node<Output = Q<Bar>>` — Queue, read via `iter_fresh()`.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AtrNode` (`bt_core::bars::AtrNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | Wilder's Average True Range over completed bars. TR = max(h−l, \|h−pc\|, \|l−pc\|) (first bar: h−l, no previous close); the first `period` TRs seed with their mean, then `atr = (atr·(p−1) + tr) / p`. Emits the running value from the first bar; initialized after `period` emissions. |
| `BarAggregator` (`bt_core::bars::BarAggregator`) | `Q<Bar>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, interval_ns: u64) -> Self` | Aggregates a `f64` stream (typically the quote mid) into fixed-interval time bars. Boundaries are aligned to the epoch origin: `open_ts = ts − ts % interval_ns`. |
| `BarCloseNode` (`bt_core::bars::BarCloseNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>) -> Self` | Extracts the close of the most recent completed bar as a `f64` State stream — the whole indicator library then runs on bar closes. |
| `TimerBarAggregator` (`bt_core::bars::TimerBarAggregator`) | `Q<Bar>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, timer: Stream<crate::graph_engine::TimerTick>, interval_ns: u64) -> Self` | [`BarAggregator`] plus an engine timer: bars close at their **exact boundary** when the timer tick arrives, not at the next market event. The timer should tick on (a multiple of) the bar interval. A firing with only a timer tick never re-folds the stale mid and never opens a phantom bar — folding requires a *fresh* mid (tracked by timestamp). Empty intervals still emit nothing. |

### `trade_bars`

Trade-price bars — real traded volume and OHLC over actual trades (klines), not the quote mid. `TradeBarToBar` adapts a `TradeBar` stream back to the plain `Bar` shape everything in `bar_indicators`/`trend_indicators` etc. consumes, so either bar family feeds the same downstream nodes.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TimerTradeBarAggregator` (`bt_core::trade_bars::TimerTradeBarAggregator`) | `Q<TradeBar>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Trade>, timer: Stream<crate::graph_engine::TimerTick>, interval_ns: u64) -> Self` | [`TradeBarAggregator`] plus an engine timer: bars close at their **exact boundary** when the tick arrives, not at the next trade. The timer should tick on (a multiple of) the bar interval — this is not enforced (there is no scheduler contract to check it against); misalignment doesn't corrupt anything, it just means the tick lands inside a bar rather than on its edge, so the close is detected late (`close_ts` is still the correct boundary — only *when* the fold notices has slipped). Queue inputs are exactly-once, so no re-fold guard is needed: a firing with only a tick folds nothing and never opens a phantom bar. |
| `TradeBarAggregator` (`bt_core::trade_bars::TradeBarAggregator`) | `Q<TradeBar>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Trade>, interval_ns: u64) -> Self` | Aggregates the trade tape into fixed-interval OHLCV bars. Boundaries are aligned to the epoch origin: `open_ts = ts − ts % interval_ns`. All fresh trades share the firing's epoch ts, so at most one bar closes per firing; a print exactly at the boundary belongs to the next bar (close-first, the `BarAggregator` rule). |
| `TradeBarToBar` (`bt_core::trade_bars::TradeBarToBar`) | `Q<Bar>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>) -> Self` | Adapter: trade bars as plain [`Bar`]s (volume dropped) so every existing bar consumer — `AtrNode`, the candle detectors — runs on the trade tape unchanged. The reverse direction is deliberately absent: mid-bars have no volume to invent. |

### `true_bar`

Gap-aware "true range" bar aggregation (`TrueBarAggregator`) — carries the previous close into the current bar's range so a gap up/down at the open is not invisible to range-based indicators.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TrueBarAggregator` (`bt_core::true_bar::TrueBarAggregator`) | `Q<TradeBar>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Trade>, interval_ns: u64, band_fraction: f64) -> Self` | Aggregates the trade tape into fixed-interval True Bars (chained open, band-VWAP close). Boundaries are epoch-aligned (`open_ts = ts − ts % interval_ns`); all fresh trades share the firing's epoch ts, so at most one bar closes per firing; a print exactly at the boundary belongs to the next bar (close-first, the `BarAggregator` rule). |

### `bar_indicators`

Classic bar-based technical indicators (ADX, Aroon, Donchian, Keltner, Swing points, CCI, fuzzy candle classification, AMAT) — every one takes a `Stream<Q<Bar>>`, i.e. the output of a bar aggregator above.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AdxNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::AdxNode`) | `Adx` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | Wilder ADX. Per diff (consecutive bar pair): `up = h − prev_h`, `down = prev_l − l`; `+DM = up` iff `up > down && up > 0` (else 0), `−DM = down` iff `down > up && down > 0`; TR as in [`AtrNode`]. TR and ±DM are Wilder-smoothed (mean seed over the first `p` diffs); `±DI = 100·±DM_s/TR_s` (TR_s == 0 → both 0); `DX = 100·\|+DI − −DI\|/(+DI + −DI)` (zero sum → 0); ADX is Wilder-smoothed DX (its own mean seed over the first `p` DX values). Emits from the second bar; conventionally stable after `2p` diffs (`warmup`). |
| `AmatNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::AmatNode`) | `Amat` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, fast: usize, slow: usize, signal_period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `AroonNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::AroonNode`) | `Aroon` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `BarCloseFieldNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::BarCloseFieldNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>) -> Self` | Bar close as a f64 stream. |
| `BarHighNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::BarHighNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>) -> Self` | Bar high as a f64 State stream. |
| `BarLowNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::BarLowNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>) -> Self` | Bar low as a f64 State stream. |
| `BarTypicalNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::BarTypicalNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>) -> Self` | Typical price `(high + low + close) / 3` as a f64 State stream. |
| `CciNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::CciNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | Commodity Channel Index over typical prices `(h+l+c)/3`: two-pass SMA and mean absolute deviation over the window (insertion order), then `(tp − sma) / (0.015·mad)`. `mad == 0` pins 0. Emits from the first full window. |
| `FuzzyNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::FuzzyNode`) | `Fuzzy` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, period: usize, threshold1: f64, threshold2: f64, threshold3: f64) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `SwingsNode` (`bt_core::bar_indicators::SwingsNode`) | `Swing` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |

### `footprint`

Order-flow footprint bars: per-price-level bid/ask traded volume within each bar, plus delta and imbalance summaries over that structure.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FootprintAggregator` (`bt_core::footprint::FootprintAggregator`) | `Q<FootprintBar>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Trade>, interval_ns: u64, bin_size_raw: i64) -> Self` | Aggregates the trade tape into fixed-interval footprint bars. Same boundary/close discipline as `TradeBarAggregator`: `open_ts = ts − ts % interval_ns`; a print at `ts >= close_ts` closes the current bar first (belongs to the next bar); at most one close per firing. |
| `FootprintDeltaNode` (`bt_core::footprint::FootprintDeltaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<FootprintBar>>) -> Self` | Last fresh bar's classified `delta` (the per-bar CVD sibling for consumers already paying for footprints — no second tape scan). |
| `ImbalanceCountNode` (`bt_core::footprint::ImbalanceCountNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<FootprintBar>>, ratio: f64, min_volume: f64) -> Self` | Net stacked diagonal-imbalance count of the last fresh bar (see [`net_stacked`]): `max_run(buy) − max_run(sell)`, signed. |

### `volume_profile`

Session and developing volume-by-price profiles (POC, value area) over trades.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DevelopingProfileNode` (`bt_core::volume_profile::DevelopingProfileNode`) | `Option<ProfileSummary>` | State | `fn new(trades: Stream<Trade>, sessions: Option<Stream<SessionEvents>>, params: &ProfileParams) -> Self` | Developing (running) profile: folds every print into the histogram and emits the recomputed summary on each firing that folded ≥ 1 print. A **tradeless** session reset (Open with no same-epoch print) emits `None` so the reset is observable and the prior session's levels stop being the latest State value — a consumer peeking between the Open and the first new print reads `None`, never a stale POC. `sessions = None` ⇒ run-anchored (never resets, never emits `None`). |
| `SessionProfileNode` (`bt_core::volume_profile::SessionProfileNode`) | `SessionProfile` | Queue | `fn new(trades: Stream<Trade>, sessions: Stream<SessionEvents>, params: &ProfileParams) -> Self` | Completed-session profile: accumulates the histogram and, at each session `Close`, emits the finished session's `SessionProfile` (summary + HVN/LVN lists) and restarts. `Close` precedes `Open` in a shared batch (the `sessions.rs` pin), and both precede same-epoch prints. An empty session emits nothing. `open_boundary` is the session `Open`'s boundary, or — when the run starts mid-session — the first print's ts (pinned fallback). |

### `compose`

Generic stream-algebra nodes usable on ANY `f64`/`bool` stream: logical (`AndNode`/`OrNode`/`NotNode`), thresholding, z-score, winsorize, lag, as-of join, cooldown, persistence, sequence/timeout, divergence.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AndNode` (`bt_core::compose::AndNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<bool>, b: Stream<bool>) -> Self` | Logical AND of two boolean streams. Same-epoch join semantics (the `AddNode2` raw fan-in pattern): fires on either input; reads both inputs' latest causal values — the boolean reflects the epoch's current state of every input, not a stale mix from whichever input happened to trigger. |
| `AsOfJoinNode` (`bt_core::compose::AsOfJoinNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(base: Stream<f64>, other: Stream<f64>, max_staleness: u32, if_missing: MissingPolicy) -> Self` | As-of join: on each `base` emission, emits the causally-latest `other` value — never a future one. `other` is a **peek** edge (readable, never wakes) so the join triggers only on `base`; raw fan-in on `other` is explicit, matching the `AndNode`/`OrNode` "peek/hold" precedent but with an explicit staleness budget instead of unconditional holding. |
| `CooldownNode` (`bt_core::compose::CooldownNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<bool>, cooldown: u32) -> Self` | Passes a `true` input through once (emitting `true` on the update it arrives), then suppresses (emits `false` unconditionally) for the next `cooldown` **updates** regardless of the input, before allowing another `true` to pass. Boundary: the update that passes `true` does NOT itself count toward the suppression window — the window is exactly the `cooldown` updates strictly after it. While the suppression counter is positive, every update decrements it by one and emits `false`, even if the input is `true` that update (a `true` arriving mid-cooldown is dropped, not queued or extended). Once the counter reaches zero, the very next `true` input passes through and re-arms a fresh `cooldown`-update window. |
| `DivergenceNode` (`bt_core::compose::DivergenceNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>) -> Self` | Sign-of-slope divergence between two streams over the last step: `true` when `a` and `b` moved in opposite directions (`a` rose while `b` fell, or vice versa) since their prior sample, else `false`. A flat move on either side (no strict rise or fall) never counts as divergence. Both edges are depth-2 triggers (this step's value and the prior one), same join semantics as [`AndNode`]/[`OrNode`] (raw fan-in, reads both inputs' latest causal values on either trigger). Boolean gate: default `derive_meta` (`Unspecified`). |
| `ForwardFillNode` (`bt_core::compose::ForwardFillNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(value: Stream<f64>, tick: Stream<Tk>, max_fill: u32) -> Self` | Multi-frequency alignment: holds the last `value` seen and re-emits it on every `tick` up to `max_fill` times since the last refresh, then emits `None` (the staleness limit — an explicit forward-fill horizon instead of filling forever). |
| `LagNode` (`bt_core::compose::LagNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, k: u32) -> Self` | Emits the value from `k` emissions ago (the `RocNode` depth-read precedent): a depth-`(k+1)` trigger edge means the node is gated until the input holds `>= k+1` elements, so `ctx.s(input)[k]` can never read out of range — no `warmup` override needed, depth gating supplies it. The first emission lands on the input's `(k+1)`-th element and carries the value of its 1st element (index `k` counting back from the newest). No lookahead is structural here: `[k]` only ever names an already-appended element, never a future one. |
| `NotNode` (`bt_core::compose::NotNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<bool>) -> Self` | Logical NOT of a boolean stream. Fires on its single input and inverts that input's latest causal value each update. |
| `OrNode` (`bt_core::compose::OrNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<bool>, b: Stream<bool>) -> Self` | Logical OR of two boolean streams. Same-epoch join semantics (the `AddNode2` raw fan-in pattern): fires on either input; reads both inputs' latest causal values — the boolean reflects the epoch's current state of every input, not a stale mix from whichever input happened to trigger. |
| `PersistenceNode` (`bt_core::compose::PersistenceNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<bool>, n: u32) -> Self` | Emits `true` only once the input has been `true` for `n` consecutive **updates** of the input (not wall-clock time) — every `on_update` call is one update, whether or not the underlying value actually changed. Boundary: on the update where the streak first reaches `n` consecutive `true`s, this emits `true` for the first time; it keeps emitting `true` on every subsequent update while the input remains `true` (the streak keeps growing past `n`, state stays latched true). Any `false` update immediately resets the streak to 0 and emits `false` that same update (a single `false` breaks the run — there is no leniency/debounce here, unlike `ThresholdNode`). |
| `RelativeChangeNode` (`bt_core::compose::RelativeChangeNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, k: u32, if_zero: f64) -> Self` | `(x[0] − x[k]) / x[k]`, with a pinned value when `x[k] == 0.0` (the `DivNode2` finite-pin precedent). This is `RocNode`'s depth-read shape with an explicit zero-pin and a `Return` unit label — a *compose* node, not a change to `RocNode`. Depth-`(k+1)` trigger edge, so `v[k]` can never read out of range; no `warmup` override needed, depth gating supplies it (mirrors [`LagNode`]). |
| `SequenceNode` (`bt_core::compose::SequenceNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<bool>, b: Stream<bool>, window: u32) -> Self` | Emits `true` on the update where `b` is `true` within `window` **updates** after `a` was last `true` — a two-trigger-edge join (same shape as `AndNode`/`OrNode`): it fires whenever either `a` or `b` emits, and reads both inputs' latest causal values every time. |
| `ThresholdNode` (`bt_core::compose::ThresholdNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, enter: f64, exit: f64, debounce: u32) -> Self` | Enter when `x >= enter`, exit when `x <= exit`, with hysteresis (`enter >= exit`) and debounce: the state only flips after `debounce` consecutive qualifying samples. Emits the boolean state every update. |
| `TimeoutNode` (`bt_core::compose::TimeoutNode`) | `bool` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<bool>, ttl: u32) -> Self` | Latches `true` when the input is `true`, holds `true` for `ttl` **updates** total (including the triggering update itself), then auto-releases to `false` unless a new `true` refreshes the countdown. Boundary: the update where input goes `true` (re)sets the countdown to `ttl` and emits `true` that same update (this counts as the first of the `ttl` held updates). Each subsequent update while latched decrements the countdown by 1 and emits `true` as long as the countdown is still > 0 after decrementing — unless refreshed by another `true` input, which resets the countdown back to `ttl` and emits `true` regardless. So for `ttl = k`, the node emits `true` on the triggering update and the next `k - 1` updates (`k` updates total), then `false` on the `k`-th update after the trigger, and stays `false` until the next `true` input. |
| `WinsorizeNode` (`bt_core::compose::WinsorizeNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> Self` | Clamps `x` to `[lo, hi]` — a static outlier guard. Clamping preserves the input's unit (a clamped price is still a price), so `derive_meta` inherits rather than relabels. |
| `ZScoreNode` (`bt_core::compose::ZScoreNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Rolling z-score: `(x − mean) / stddev` over the trailing `period` samples (the `StdDevNode` two-pass mean/stddev math). A flat window (`stddev == 0.0`) pins `0.0` — the "no deviation, no signal" reading, matching the `DivNode2`/`Stochastic` zero-denominator precedent. `warmup` = 1: the first emission is already a full-window score. |

### `exec`

Executor-facing nodes (basket/target-position execution bookkeeping) — engine-internal lanes, not the single-instrument authoring path.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BasketExecutor` (`bt_core::exec::BasketExecutor`) | `Vec<Cmd>` | Queue | `fn new(cmds_in: Stream<Commands>, reports: Stream<ExecReport>, quotes: Vec<Stream<Quote>>, instruments: Vec<Instrument>, policy: PartialPolicy, style: ExecStyle) -> Self` | [`TargetPositionExecutor`] across a basket: one slot (tracker, target, attempt budget) per instrument, one shared [`PartialPolicy`]. `Cmd::TargetFor` routes by instrument id (an unknown id is a config bug and panics — fail fast); bare `Cmd::Target` means instrument 0, the exact single-instrument behavior. Fills route to slots by the fill's own instrument id, so manual strategy orders count toward the position an executor reconciles against — same semantics as the single executor. Stand-downs emit [`Residual`]s. |
| `TargetPositionExecutor` (`bt_core::exec::TargetPositionExecutor`) | `Vec<Cmd>` | Queue | `fn new(cmds_in: Stream<Commands>, reports: Stream<ExecReport>, quotes: Stream<Quote>, instrument: Instrument, policy: PartialPolicy, style: ExecStyle) -> Self` | Interposed policy node (spec §8.3): consumes the strategy's command stream, passes raw commands through verbatim, and reconciles `Cmd::Target` desired state with market IOC orders (v1 market-only). The idempotence guard: nothing is sent while an order is in flight — re-emitting the same target never duplicates orders. |

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |

| `AddNode2` (`bt_core::nodes::AddNode2`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>) -> Self` | `a + b` (join: fires when either emits, reads both latest). |
| `AmaNode` (`bt_core::nodes::AmaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize, fast: usize, slow: usize) -> Self` | Kaufman Adaptive Moving Average. `ER` over `period` (same rolling `period + 1`-price window as `EfficiencyRatioNode`); smoothing constant `sc = (ER·(fast_sc − slow_sc) + slow_sc)²` with `fast_sc = 2/(fast+1)`, `slow_sc = 2/(slow+1)`. Seed `value = x` on the first input, then `value += sc·(x − value)`. |
| `CmoNode` (`bt_core::nodes::CmoNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Chande Momentum Oscillator over the last `period` diffs: `100·(Σgains − Σlosses)/(Σgains + Σlosses)`. Both-zero window pins `0.0`. |
| `DivNode2` (`bt_core::nodes::DivNode2`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>, if_zero: f64) -> Self` | `a / b` (join), with a pinned value when `b == 0.0` (matches `-0.0` too) — division-by-zero edges get documented values, never NaN propagation (spec §4). The pinned value is a build-time parameter and enters the CSE key as bits. |
| `EfficiencyRatioNode` (`bt_core::nodes::EfficiencyRatioNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Kaufman Efficiency Ratio over `period`: `\|x[0] − x[period]\| / Σ_{i=1..period} \|x[i−1] − x[i]\|`, computed over a rolling window of `period + 1` prices. Flat window (zero denominator) pins `0.0`. Standalone, independently-tested node — `AmaNode::er()` reimplements this same computation inline rather than consuming it. |
| `EmaNode` (`bt_core::nodes::EmaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | EMA, Nautilus contract: seed on first input, then `alpha.mul_add(x, (1-alpha)*value)` (FMA); warmup = period. |
| `LrNode` (`bt_core::nodes::LrNode`) | `LrState` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `MidNode` (`bt_core::nodes::MidNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Quote>) -> Self` | Quote mid: exact integer midpoint of the raws, as f64 (`extract_price(Mid)` semantics from the differential contract). |
| `MulNode2` (`bt_core::nodes::MulNode2`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>) -> Self` | `a · b` (join: fires when either emits, reads both latest). |
| `PslNode` (`bt_core::nodes::PslNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Psychological Line: `100 · (#{up diffs} in the last period) / period`. |
| `RmaNode` (`bt_core::nodes::RmaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Wilder moving average (SMMA): seed = SMA of the first `period` inputs, then `rma = (rma·(p−1) + x)/p`. This is the same smoothing shape inlined in `RsiNode`, as its own standalone, independently-tested node. (Note: `RviNode` inlines its own separate Wilder recurrence — `up_s`/`down_s` — rather than constructing or consuming this node.) |
| `RocNode` (`bt_core::nodes::RocNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Rate of change over `p` emissions: `(x[0] − x[p]) / x[p]`. Stateless — the depth-read showcase: history comes from the declared input depth, readiness gating supplies the warmup. |
| `RollingMaxNode` (`bt_core::nodes::RollingMaxNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `RollingMinNode` (`bt_core::nodes::RollingMinNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `RsiNode` (`bt_core::nodes::RsiNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Wilder RSI: avg gain/loss seeded by the mean of the first `p` diffs, then Wilder smoothing `avg = (avg·(p−1) + x) / p`. All-loss → 0, all-gain → 100. |
| `RviNode` (`bt_core::nodes::RviNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize, smoothing: usize) -> Self` | Relative Volatility Index: RSI applied to the rolling standard deviation of price. Each bar `σ = StdDev(close, period)`; if close rose vs the prior close `up = σ, down = 0`, else `up = 0, down = σ`. Both are Wilder-smoothed over `smoothing`; `rvi = 100·up_s/(up_s + down_s)`, both-zero pins `50.0`. |
| `ScaleNode` (`bt_core::nodes::ScaleNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, k: f64) -> Self` | `k · x`, `k` a build-time parameter (enters the cse key as bits). |
| `SmaNode` (`bt_core::nodes::SmaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Simple moving average: two-pass sum over the window each emission. |
| `StdDevNode` (`bt_core::nodes::StdDevNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Rolling population standard deviation, two-pass (mean, then Σ(x−μ)²/p). |
| `SubNode2` (`bt_core::nodes::SubNode2`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>) -> Self` | `a − b`. |
| `VhfNode` (`bt_core::nodes::VhfNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Vertical Horizontal Filter over the last `period` closes: `\|max − min\| / Σ\|Δclose\|`. Zero path length pins `0.0`. |
| `VidyaNode` (`bt_core::nodes::VidyaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Variable Index Dynamic Average: `cmo_pct = \|CMO(x, p)\| / 100`, `alpha = 2/(p+1)`, `value = alpha·cmo_pct·x + (1 − alpha·cmo_pct)·value`, seeded `value = x` on the first input. `cmo_pct` reimplements, inline, the same fixed rolling `period`-diff CMO arithmetic pinned by `CmoNode` (Task 3's pinned definition) as its own standalone, independently-tested computation — it does not construct or consume a `CmoNode`. |
| `WmaNode` (`bt_core::nodes::WmaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Linearly-weighted moving average: weights 1..=p, newest heaviest. |

### `patterns`

Chart/candlestick pattern and structural-level detectors — see the sub-table below. Every detector's `Output` is `Vec<PatternEvent<P>>` (`PatternEvents<P>`), a **Queue** stream: episodes with a `Stage` (`Forming`/`Confirmed`/`Invalidated`/`Completed`) consumed via `iter_fresh()`, never indexed.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BreakoutDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::BreakoutDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Breakout>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, lookback: usize, approach_frac: f64, target_mult: f64, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | Resistance-breakout detector over an `f64` stream (typically the quote mid or a close). One live episode at a time; ids increment. |
| `Canonicalize` (`bt_core::patterns::canonical::Canonicalize`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<CanonicalEpisode>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<PatternEvents<P>>, kind: &str, map: impl Trait) -> Self` | Maps `Stream<PatternEvents<P>>` to `Stream<CanonicalEvents>`, one episode at a time, preserving the event envelope verbatim. |
| `CupAndHandleDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::cup::CupAndHandleDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<ChartPattern>>` | Queue | `fn new(pivots_in: Stream<Q<Pivot>>, price_in: Stream<f64>, params: CupParams, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `DojiDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::candle::DojiDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Candle>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, params: DojiParams, trend_lookback: usize, follow_through: usize) -> Self` | Recommended: `trend_lookback = 0` (a doji needs no context). A nonzero `trend_lookback` does not gate anything here — the doji classifier ignores trend entirely — it only enlarges the rolling window and delays the first possible detection. |
| `DoubleDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::chart::DoubleDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<ChartPattern>>` | Queue | `fn new(pivots_in: Stream<Q<Pivot>>, price_in: Stream<f64>, kind: DoubleKind, params: DoubleParams, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | Spec §4.2: two same-side pivots within a price tolerance, confirmed on break of the intervening valley/peak, target = height projected. `Bottom` runs the same topology in mirror space. |
| `EngulfingDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::candle::EngulfingDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Candle>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, kind: EngulfKind, trend_lookback: usize, follow_through: usize) -> Self` | Recommended: `trend_lookback = 3`, `follow_through = 5`. |
| `FibZoneDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::levels::FibZoneDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<FibZone>>` | Queue | `fn new(pivots_in: Stream<Q<Pivot>>, price_in: Stream<f64>, levels: Vec<f64>, zone_tol: f64, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | Spec §5.3: anchored on the last confirmed swing (adjacent opposite-kind pivot pair — a same-kind pivot leaves the previous leg in place). Per zone touch: `Forming` on entry (side of entry is not tracked — Forming fires whenever the price sits inside a zone with no live episode), `Confirmed` on the trend-side exit (terminal; there is no Completed stage), `Invalidated` on the far-side exit or when a new swing re-anchors the zones. Zones are checked in configured level order; validation guarantees they never overlap, so at most one contains the price. |
| `FlagDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::chart::FlagDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<ChartPattern>>` | Queue | `fn new(pivots_in: Stream<Q<Pivot>>, price_in: Stream<f64>, dir: SignalDir, params: FlagParams, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | Spec §4.3: impulse pole (consecutive Low→High pivot pair with rise ≥ threshold) followed by a counter-trend drift; confirmed on a break beyond the pole tip in the pole direction after a proven pull-back. |
| `GapDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::gaps::GapDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Gap>>` | Queue | `fn new(sessions_in: Stream<SessionEvents>, price_in: Stream<f64>, threshold: f64, runaway: f64) -> Self` | Spec §5.3: session open vs prior session close beyond `threshold` (fraction of the prior close) ⇒ `Confirmed` immediately (no Forming stage); `Completed` on gap fill; `Invalidated` on extension beyond the runaway level or at the session's own close (an unresolved fade dies with its session — the CandleEngine-timeout precedent). Empty sessions emit no events, so the prior close persists across weekends/holidays to the next session with data. |
| `HammerDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::candle::HammerDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Candle>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, kind: HammerKind, params: HammerParams, trend_lookback: usize, follow_through: usize) -> Self` | Recommended: `trend_lookback = 3`, `follow_through = 5`. |
| `HaramiDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::candle::HaramiDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Harami>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, kind: HaramiKind, params: HaramiParams, trend_lookback: usize, follow_through: usize) -> Self` | Recommended: `trend_lookback = 3`, `follow_through = 5`. |
| `HeadAndShouldersDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::chart::HeadAndShouldersDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<ChartPattern>>` | Queue | `fn new(pivots_in: Stream<Q<Pivot>>, price_in: Stream<f64>, params: HnsParams, inverse: bool, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | Spec §4.2. Regular topology is bearish (break DOWN through the neckline); `inverse = true` detects the bullish mirror. |
| `PiercingDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::candle::PiercingDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Candle>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, kind: PierceKind, params: PierceParams, trend_lookback: usize, follow_through: usize) -> Self` | Recommended: `trend_lookback = 3`, `follow_through = 5`. |
| `PivotNode` (`bt_core::patterns::pivots::PivotNode`) | `Q<Pivot>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, k: usize) -> Self` | Emits a [`Pivot`] when the center of the last `2k+1` elements is a strict extreme versus all `2k` neighbors. Strictness means plateaus (equal extremes) never emit — ambiguous structure is skipped rather than guessed at. |
| `RangeDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::levels::RangeDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<RangeData>>` | Queue | `fn new(pivots_in: Stream<Q<Pivot>>, price_in: Stream<f64>, m: usize, band_tol: f64) -> Self` | Spec §4.5: `m` consecutive pivots inside a band of width ≤ `band_tol · mid` ⇒ Confirmed when the box qualifies; Completed on exit (either side, direction in the event data). No Invalidated stage. |
| `SessionLevelsNode` (`bt_core::patterns::gaps::SessionLevelsNode`) | `Q<SessionLevels>` | Queue | `fn new(sessions_in: Stream<SessionEvents>, price_in: Stream<f64>) -> Self` | Spec §5.3: emits the PRIOR session's high/low as a level stream at each session open (a plain Queue like [`super::pivots::Pivot`] — levels are infrastructure, not detection episodes). The first session with data emits nothing (no prior); empty sessions are skipped naturally (no Open, no emission, stats persist). |
| `SoldiersCrowsDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::candle::SoldiersCrowsDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Candle>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, kind: MarchKind, params: MarchParams, trend_lookback: usize, follow_through: usize) -> Self` | Recommended: `trend_lookback = 0` (no trend gate — see [`MarchParams`]), `follow_through = 5`. |
| `StarDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::candle::StarDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Candle>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, kind: StarKind, params: StarParams, trend_lookback: usize, follow_through: usize) -> Self` | Recommended: `trend_lookback = 3`, `follow_through = 5`. |
| `SupportBounceDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::levels::SupportBounceDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<Bounce>>` | Queue | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, lookback: usize, approach_frac: f64, bounce_frac: f64, target_mult: f64, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | Mirror of the resistance breakout: approach a prior-window low from above, hold, confirm on a bounce ≥ `bounce_frac` of the window range. A bounce requires an approach — there is no immediate-confirm path. |
| `TriangleDetector` (`bt_core::patterns::chart::TriangleDetector`) | `Vec<PatternEvent<ChartPattern>>` | Queue | `fn new(pivots_in: Stream<Q<Pivot>>, price_in: Stream<f64>, kind: TriangleKind, params: TriangleParams, emit_forming: bool) -> Self` | Spec §4.3: trendline fit over 2 highs + 2 lows converging per kind; confirmed on boundary break (trend side for Asc/Desc, either side for Sym), invalidated on re-cross. |

### `portfolio`

Portfolio construction and reconciliation nodes: forecast blending/weighting, group caps, constraints, rebalancing, target-quantity reconciliation.

| `ConstraintNode` (`bt_core::portfolio::constraints::ConstraintNode`) | `TargetPortfolio` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<TargetPortfolio>, max_name: f64, max_gross: f64) -> Self` | Converts a `TargetPortfolio` into a constraint-compliant `TargetPortfolio` (design §8.5): the primary enforcement point between `WeightNode`'s raw target weights and downstream rebalance/reconcile nodes (later tasks). Triggers on the `TargetPortfolio` stream; emits `None` only when the input itself is `None`/empty (an empty portfolio trivially satisfies every cap, but there's nothing to emit — mirrors `WeightNode`'s empty-ranking `None` rule, not its empty-portfolio `Some(empty)` rule, because here "empty" can only come from an upstream `None`/empty portfolio, never from this node's own math). |
| `ForecastNode` (`bt_core::portfolio::forecast::ForecastNode`) | `Forecast` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<T>, subject_slot: usize, target: &str, model_version: &str, horizon_offset: u64, expiry_offset: u64, confidence: f64) -> Self` | Annotate a value stream as a `Forecast` (analogous to `FeatureNode` annotating a `Feature<T>`): reads the latest value each epoch and derives `point` (= value), `magnitude` (= `\|value\|`), and `direction` (sign of value, via `Direction::from_weight`) from it. `horizon`/ `expiry` are `ctx.clock()` plus the ctor-provided offsets; `as_of` is always `ctx.clock()` (the firing epoch). |
| `GroupCapNode` (`bt_core::portfolio::constraints::GroupCapNode`) | `TargetPortfolio` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<TargetPortfolio>, groups: Vec<u32>, max_group_gross: f64) -> Self` | Converts a `TargetPortfolio` into a per-group-gross-capped `TargetPortfolio` (design §11 sector/country/factor limits): the concrete, generic stand-in for those named taxonomies -- callers map their own sector/country/factor labels onto the fixed `groups: Vec<u32>` slot map. Sibling of `ConstraintNode` (same file, same `TargetPortfolio -> TargetPortfolio` shape, same trigger/empty/ non-finite conventions); the two nodes are independent and compose by chaining, not by one calling the other. |
| `RebalanceNode` (`bt_core::portfolio::rebalance::RebalanceNode`) | `TargetPortfolio` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<TargetPortfolio>, n: usize, caps: Constraints, band: f64, max_turnover: f64) -> Self` | See module docs for the full protocol, emission-disposition rule, and attribution/CSE notes. |

| `VolTargetNode` (`bt_core::portfolio::vol_target::VolTargetNode`) | `TargetPortfolio` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<TargetPortfolio>, forecasts: Vec<Stream<Forecast>>, target_vol: f64, max_multiplier: f64, expected_target: &str, stale_policy: StalePolicy, max_warmup: Option<u64>) -> Self` | Converts a `TargetPortfolio` into a vol-target-scaled `TargetPortfolio`. See the module docs for the full contract. |

| `FlowImbNode` (`bt_core::signals::flowimb::FlowImbNode`) | `Forecast` | State | `fn new(clock: Stream<Clk>, qi_s: Stream<f64>, pressure: Stream<Pressure>, qi_min: f64, pressure_min: f64, cap: f64, horizon_offset: u64, expiry_offset: u64, subject_slot: usize, max_pressure_age_ns: Option<u64>) -> Self` | Ensemble combiner (design §3.4): triggers on `clock`, peeks the smoothed signed queue imbalance and the trade `Pressure`, and emits a directional [`Forecast`] iff both channels agree in sign and clear their magnitude floors. `point` is the bounded queue-imbalance channel; pressure is the confirming gate + a confidence factor. |
| `FreshnessNode` (`bt_core::signals::xsmom::FreshnessNode`) | `Membership` | State | `fn new(values: Vec<Stream<f64>>, clock: Stream<Clk>, max_age_ns: u64) -> Self` | Freshness-driven membership: a slot is an active member iff its value stream has emitted at least once AND its latest element is no older than `max_age_ns` at the current clock epoch. This is the staleness bound the latching cross-section snapshot deliberately does not have (`CrossSectionNode` peeks State streams, which hold their last value forever): without it, one dead feed's score would stay eligible for ranking indefinitely while a live clock keeps snapshotting — a stale leader/laggard could be traded forever (adversarial-review finding, design §9). |
| `HorizonMomentumNode` (`bt_core::signals::tsmom::HorizonMomentumNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<f64>, lookback: usize, score_cap: f64) -> Self` | Vol-normalized momentum score over one lookback: the t-statistic-style `sum(r) / (sigma_pop(r) * sqrt(n))` of the last `n` log returns, clamped to `[-score_cap, +score_cap]`. |
| `PairsRevNode` (`bt_core::signals::pairsrev::PairsRevNode`) | `PairsRevSignal` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>, beta: Stream<f64>, corr: Stream<f64>, z_period: usize, z_entry: f64, z_cap: f64, min_corr: f64, horizon_offset: u64, expiry_offset: u64) -> Self` | Residual-reversion classifier (design §3.3). Per epoch: gate on β/ρ warmup and `ρ >= min_corr` (structural break -> silence + residual window RESET — residuals from a broken regime are not a baseline for the reformed one), compute `r = a − β·b`, score it against the trailing exclude-current window (`z = clamp((r−mean)/σ_pop, ±z_cap)`; σ == 0 pins ±z_cap on nonzero deviation, 0.0 otherwise — the exact `BarShockNode` rule), and emit on `\|z\| >= z_entry`. |
| `ShockRevNode` (`bt_core::signals::shockrev::ShockRevNode`) | `Forecast` | State | `fn new(shock: Stream<f64>, rel_vol: Stream<f64>, z_min: f64, rv_low: f64, rv_high: f64, score_cap: f64, horizon_offset: u64, expiry_offset: u64, subject_slot: usize) -> Self` | Band-rule combiner emitting the standard [`Forecast`] (design §3.4). Per epoch where both inputs are fresh, with `zc = clamp(z, ±score_cap)` (the node is public and accepts arbitrary streams, so it clamps defensively even though [`BarShockNode`] already caps its output): |
| `SignedQueueImbalanceNode` (`bt_core::signals::flowimb::SignedQueueImbalanceNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Quote>) -> Self` | Signed top-of-book queue imbalance `(bid_size - ask_size) / (bid_size + ask_size)` in `[-1, 1]` (positive = bid-heavy). Empty book (`bid + ask == 0`) pins `0.0`. Distinct from the UNSIGNED `ImbalanceNode` (`min/max` balance ∈ [0,1]). |
| `TsMomNode` (`bt_core::signals::tsmom::TsMomNode`) | `Forecast` | State | `fn new(scores: Vec<Stream<f64>>, lookbacks: Vec<usize>, regime: Stream<f64>, min_regime: f64, horizon_offset: u64, expiry_offset: u64, subject_slot: usize) -> Self` | Multi-horizon combiner + regime qualifier emitting the standard [`Forecast`] (design §5.3). Per firing epoch, with per-horizon scores `s_i` and efficiency ratio `e`: |
| `VolBreakNode` (`bt_core::signals::volbreak::VolBreakNode`) | `Forecast` | State | `fn new(bars: Stream<Q<Bar>>, bb_width: Stream<f64>, kc_width: Stream<f64>, dc_up: Stream<f64>, dc_lo: Stream<f64>, min_squeeze: usize, break_lookback: usize, score_cap: f64, horizon_offset: u64, expiry_offset: u64, subject_slot: usize) -> Self` | Squeeze-run classifier (design §3.3). Triggers on `bars`; peeks the Bollinger width, Keltner width, and the ONE-BAR-LAGGED Donchian range legs (so the break compares the current close against the prior range). |
| `XsMomNode` (`bt_core::signals::xsmom::XsMomNode`) | `ForecastSet` | State | `fn new(ranking: Stream<Ranking>, k: usize, raw_min: f64, score_cap: f64, min_breadth: usize, horizon_offset: u64, expiry_offset: u64) -> Self` | Rank-rule combiner (design §3.4): per fresh [`Ranking`], gate on breadth and cross-sectional dispersion, then select `top(k)` / `bottom(k)` members that pass both the time-series strength gate (`\|raw\| >= raw_min` — rank position without own-series momentum is rank noise) and the z-sign gate (a top-k slot at/below the cross-sectional mean, possible for k >= 2 with a skewed section, carries no positive relative edge; mirrored for bottom-k). |

### `trend_indicators`

Trend-following overlays: SuperTrend, PSAR, Ichimoku.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `IchimokuNode` (`bt_core::trend_indicators::IchimokuNode`) | `Ichimoku` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, t: usize, k: usize, s: usize) -> Self` | Rolling high-low midpoints: Tenkan over `t` bars, Kijun over `k`, Senkou B raw over `s`; Senkou A raw = `(tenkan + kijun)/2`. Raw senkou values enter a FIFO and surface `k` bars later (the raw computed at bar `i` applies at bar `i + k`). Emits only when all four lines are defined — first at bar `k + max(t, k, s)` bars (typically `s + k`). Midpoint op order: `(max + min) / 2`, extremes by two-pass comparison. |
| `PsarNode` (`bt_core::trend_indicators::PsarNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, af_start: f64, af_step: f64, af_max: f64) -> Self` | Wilder Parabolic SAR. Seeded from the first two bars: direction Up iff `c2 >= c1`; seed SAR = the two bars' extreme against the trend (min low for Up / max high for Down), seed EP = the extreme with it. Per later bar: `sar' = sar + af·(ep − sar)`, then clamped so an uptrend SAR never exceeds the prior two lows (downtrend: never below the prior two highs). Price crossing SAR reverses: the reversal bar emits the prior EP **unclamped**, direction flips, af resets. A new extreme advances EP and grows af by `af_step` up to `af_max`. Emits from the second bar. |
| `SuperTrendNode` (`bt_core::trend_indicators::SuperTrendNode`) | `SuperTrend` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<Bar>>, period: usize, mult: f64) -> Self` | Classic ratcheting SuperTrend over Wilder ATR (the exact [`crate::bars::AtrNode`] recurrence, folded internally so bands and ATR share one pass). |

### `volume_indicators`

Volume-weighted indicators: VWAP, OBV, A/D line, Chaikin/KVO, MFI, relative volume, trade-bar volume.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AdLineNode` (`bt_core::volume_indicators::AdLineNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>) -> Self` | Accumulation/Distribution line: `CLV·volume` cumulative, with `CLV = ((c − l) − (h − c)) / (h − l)` and `h == l` pinned to 0 (spec §4.3). Emits every bar; sum in arrival order. |
| `KvoNode` (`bt_core::volume_indicators::KvoNode`) | `Kvo` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>, fast: usize, slow: usize, signal_period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `MfiNode` (`bt_core::volume_indicators::MfiNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | Money Flow Index over typical-price money flow `tp·vol`, ±split by tp direction vs the prior bar (equal tp contributes zero to both sides — the window stays time-aligned). Over the last `p` diffs (two-pass, insertion order): both sums zero → **50** (RSI's 0/0 convention); zero negative-flow sum → 100; otherwise `100 − 100/(1 + pos/neg)` (all-negative falls out as 0). Emits from the first full window (`p+1` bars). |
| `ObvNode` (`bt_core::volume_indicators::ObvNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>) -> Self` | On-Balance Volume: close vs prior close signs the bar's volume into a cumulative sum (equal closes add exactly 0 — spec §4.3). Standard close-to-close; no trade-direction inference. Seeds 0 at the first bar; emits every bar. Sum order is bar-arrival order. |
| `PressureNode` (`bt_core::volume_indicators::PressureNode`) | `Pressure` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | *(no rustdoc summary — see source)* |
| `TradeBarVolumeNode` (`bt_core::volume_indicators::TradeBarVolumeNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>) -> Self` | Trade-bar volume as a f64 State stream (field extractor). |
| `VwapNode` (`bt_core::volume_indicators::VwapNode`) | `Option<f64>` | State | `fn rolling(input: Stream<Q<TradeBar>>, period: usize) -> Self` | VWAP over trade bars: `Σ(typical·vol)/Σ(vol)` with `typical = (h+l+c)/3`. Zero cumulative volume → **no emission** (spec §4.3), never NaN. Sums run in insertion order (rolling: two-pass per emission; session: cumulative in arrival order). |

### `xsection`

Cross-sectional nodes over a universe: ranking, demeaning, rolling beta/correlation, group demean.

| Node | Output | `PayloadKind` | Constructor | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CrossSectionNode` (`bt_core::xsection::snapshot::CrossSectionNode`) | `XSection` | State | `fn new(values: Vec<Stream<f64>>, membership: Option<Stream<Membership>>, clock: Stream<Clk>, min_members: usize) -> Self` | Snapshot the declared universe on each `clock` tick. Value streams and membership are PEEK edges (a not-yet-listed member never blocks readiness); only `clock` triggers. A slot is present iff it is an active member AND its value stream holds a causal value this epoch. Emits `None` (no output this tick) if fewer than `min_members` slots are present (completeness policy, design §10.2). |
| `DemeanNode` (`bt_core::xsection::neutralize::DemeanNode`) | `XSection` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<XSection>) -> Self` | Subtract the cross-sectional mean of present members from each present member (missing slots stay `None`). Output is a neutralized `XSection`. Emits `None` when the snapshot has no present members. |
| `GroupDemeanNode` (`bt_core::xsection::neutralize::GroupDemeanNode`) | `XSection` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<XSection>, groups: Vec<u32>) -> Self` | Subtract the per-group cross-sectional mean, using a fixed slot->group map declared at build time (group ids are small integers). A group with one present member neutralizes to 0.0; missing slots stay `None`. Emits `None` when the snapshot has no present members. |
| `RankNode` (`bt_core::xsection::ranking::RankNode`) | `Ranking` | State | `fn new(input: Stream<XSection>, order: RankOrder) -> Self` | Turn a per-epoch `XSection` into a `Ranking` (design §8.4): cross-sectional mean + population-stddev z-score, deterministic rank/tie-break, and percentile. Absent slots are excluded from `entries` and counted in `n_missing`. Emits `None` when the snapshot has no eligible members. |
| `RollingBetaNode` (`bt_core::xsection::stats::RollingBetaNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Rolling beta of `a` on `b`: `cov(a, b) / var(b)` (population, two-pass) over the last `period` paired samples (see module docs for pairing semantics). Degenerate: `var(b) == 0.0` (flat `b` window) pins `0.0` rather than dividing by zero. |
| `RollingCorrelationNode` (`bt_core::xsection::stats::RollingCorrelationNode`) | `f64` | State | `fn new(a: Stream<f64>, b: Stream<f64>, period: usize) -> Self` | Rolling Pearson correlation of `a` and `b` over the last `period` paired samples (paired at the union of update epochs — see module docs). Two-pass (means, then cross/variance sums) in insertion order for determinism. Degenerate: if either side's variance is exactly `0.0` (a flat window), correlation is undefined — pinned to `0.0` rather than `NaN`. |
